_notes: HOW TO USE: copy this file to public/data/questions/<your-test-id>.json, replace the dummy questions, delete this _notes block (optional), then add an entry in master.json (see templates/master-test-entry.json).
testId must be the same as the test's "id" in master.json.
type: "single_choice" (one answer, use "answer": index) | "multiple_choice" (use "answers": [indexes]) | "essay" (AI graded, no options).
Option indexes start at 0: A=0, B=1, C=2, D=3. Spread correct answers across A-D.
marks / negativeMarks / partialMarks on a question are OPTIONAL — leave them out to use the markingScheme below.
section must match an id in "sections". Questions are shown section by section in the order of "sections".

i18n: give both "hi" and "en" with the SAME number of options in the SAME order. The toggle EN/हिंदी appears only when both exist. The top-level question/options/explanation should be the same as the original language.
Or skip i18n and run: npm run translate -- <your-file>.json

en.question: Which of these are stages of Piaget's cognitive development? (Select all that apply)
en.explanation: Piaget's four stages: sensorimotor, preoperational, concrete operational and formal operational. The 'oral stage' belongs to Freud's theory.

questions.question: 12 और 18 का लघुत्तम समापवर्त्य (LCM) क्या है?
questions.explanation: 12 = 2² × 3, 18 = 2 × 3², इसलिए LCM = 2² × 3² = 36। (यह प्रश्न दिखाता है कि किसी एक प्रश्न के अंक अलग कैसे रखें: +4 / −1)

questions.question: बाल विकास में खेल की भूमिका का वर्णन कीजिए।
questions.explanation: मुख्य बिंदु: (1) शारीरिक विकास — मांसपेशियाँ और समन्वय; (2) सामाजिक विकास — सहयोग, नियम मानना, मित्रता; (3) संज्ञानात्मक विकास — समस्या समाधान, कल्पना; (4) भावनात्मक विकास — आत्मविश्वास, भावनाओं की अभिव्यक्ति; (5) भाषा विकास — संवाद और शब्दावली।

en.question: Describe the role of play in child development.
en.explanation: Key points: (1) physical development — muscles and coordination; (2) social development — cooperation, following rules, friendship; (3) cognitive development — problem solving, imagination; (4) emotional development — confidence, expressing feelings; (5) language development — communication and vocabulary.
